田中土佐.note: Tanaka Tosa (Genba), a chief retainer of the Aizu domain during its years as Kyoto Protector; he died by his own hand at the fall of Aizu in 1868.

東雲大夫.note: A tayū of the Kizuya house in Shimabara; Toshizō’s partner on the one night the chapter turns on. Dayū is the title of the first rank of courtesan.

米沢藤次.note: A Chōshū samurai and Osae’s lover in Kyoto, through whom she passed shogunate-side intelligence.

鴻池善右衛門.note: The head, by hereditary name, of the Kōnoike house, the greatest merchant-bank of Osaka (see ch15). It bankrolled Kondō in return for the corps’s protection against loyalist extortion.

大谷刑部.note: Ōtani Yoshitsugu (1559–1600), Hideyoshi’s trusted general, renowned for the handling of large forces; see the note here.

姫路.note: The castle town of Banshū (Harima), west of Osaka.

藤吉.note: The manservant (komono) attending Toshizō on the rainy night of the ambush.

ch31.anchor: went also by the name of Fudōdō-mura
ch31.note: The corps’s grandest and last barracks, at Fudōdō-mura by Shichijō-Horikawa, a walled compound with a drill-ground, said to have housed some two hundred men. Historically the Shinsengumi did not move there until 1867 (before that they were billeted at the Nishi-Honganji); Shiba brings the move forward to set this night here.

The Kōnoike were the richest merchant-bankers of Osaka, lenders to daimyō and shogunate alike (see ch15). Self-styled loyalist rōnin preyed on such houses with forced ‘war-chest’ loans; to be rid of them the Kōnoike paid the Shinsengumi for protection, and the money went, as Shiba notes with some dryness, into Kondō’s pleasures. It is a small clear picture of how the corps was kept.

Ōtani Yoshitsugu (1559–1600), Hideyoshi’s able and much-loved general, later a stalwart of the losing side at Sekigahara. A famous anecdote has Hideyoshi say that he should like to give Ōtani a hundred thousand men and watch him wield them — the highest praise for a commander’s grip on a great army. For the Aizu officer to reach for it in speaking of Toshizō is to rank his generalship above Kondō’s.
